recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Confit Tomatoes and Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised chicken is artfully arranged on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate, leaving ample white space. Two generous chunks of tender, dark-meat chicken, with crisped, golden-brown skin, rest beside a mound of coarsely smashed, creamy potatoes. Scattered around are vibrant, deeply red confit tomato halves, glistening with olive oil. A rich, dark braising liquid, subtly infused with fermented garlic, pools elegantly at the base. The dish is simply garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped chives. The presentation is clean, unfussy, highlighting the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. The plate sits on a light, textured stone surface, with an undyed linen napkin, under soft natural light, and a blurred backdrop of subtle green foliage.

ingredients.name: Fermented garlic paste or fermented chili paste (optional)

instructions: Prepare Chicken: Debone chicken thighs. Reserve bones for stock. Pat chicken skin dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Make Chicken Stock (Zero Waste): Place reserved chicken bones in a small pot. Cover with water. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain broth. Set aside.

Sear Chicken: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear until skin is crispy and golden brown, about 8-10 minutes. Flip. Sear other side 2 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: Add sliced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and fermented garlic/chili paste (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Braise Chicken: Return chicken to the pot. Add chicken stock and half of the rosemary/thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cover. Reduce heat to low. Braise 30 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.

Prepare Confit Tomatoes: While chicken braises, halve tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish or pot. Cover with remaining olive oil. Add remaining rosemary/thyme. Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 45-60 minutes, until softened and slightly shriveled. Alternatively, simmer gently on stovetop.
Cook Potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Finish Potatoes: Mash potatoes coarsely with a fork or potato masher. Season with salt and pepper. Add butter if desired.
Finish Braise: Remove chicken from pot. Shred or cut into large chunks. Reduce braising liquid slightly if too thin. Adjust seasoning. Return chicken to sauce.
Plate: Place a scoop of smashed potatoes on each plate. Spoon braised chicken and confit tomatoes next to it. Drizzle with braising liquid. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainable cooking by utilizing chicken bones for stock (zero-waste) and incorporating preserved elements like confit tomatoes. Using fermented garlic paste adds depth of flavor and incorporates a fermented ingredient into the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta with Roasted Squash and Miso-Pumpkin Seed Pesto
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of pasta is centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone. The al dente pasta is coated in a light green, creamy miso-pumpkin seed pesto. Roasted squash cubes, golden-brown with slight caramelization, are scattered throughout the dish, retaining their distinct shape. A small, vibrant pile of thinly sliced pickled red onions rests delicately on top, providing a striking pink-purple contrast. A few fresh green parsley leaves or microgreens are artfully placed as a natural garnish. The composition is clean and uncrowded, with ample white space around the dish. Natural textures of the pasta, soft squash, and crisp pickled onions are evident. The setting features a light reclaimed wood or stone table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is simply folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene. The background is minimalist, with a blurred, subtle green plant adding an eco-conscious touch.
instructions: Prepare pickled red onions. Combine thinly sliced red onion, 60ml apple cider vinegar, 60ml water, 5g sugar, and 2g salt in a small jar. Shake well. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel butternut squash. Deseed. Cut squash into 2cm cubes. Toss cubes with 20ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast squash for 25-30 minutes. Squash should be tender and slightly caramelized.
While squash roasts, prepare pesto. In a food processor, combine pumpkin seeds, white miso paste, nutritional yeast, garlic, and lemon juice. Pulse until finely chopped.
With processor running, slowly drizzle in 60ml olive oil until a smooth pesto forms. Add 30-60ml water as needed to reach desired consistency.
Cook pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water before draining.
Add drained pasta to a large bowl. Add pesto and roasted squash. Toss to combine.
Add reserved pasta water gradually to create a creamy sauce. Season with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with a spoonful of pickled red onions and optional fresh parsley or microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle with Creamy Mushroom Ragu
recipes.visual_description: The Pappardelle with Creamy Mushroom Ragu is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The wide, flat ribbons of pappardelle are loosely coiled, forming a natural, organic mound. Rich, creamy mushroom sauce clings to every strand. Abundant pieces of seared wild mushrooms, irregularly sliced or torn, are nestled throughout the pasta, showcasing their golden-brown edges. The sauce is a warm, earthy beige, flecked with darker porcini bits. A generous sprinkle of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano lightly dusts the top, providing a pale contrast. Bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the cheese, adding a vibrant pop of color. The pasta appears tender, the mushrooms offer a mix of meaty and tender textures, and the sauce looks luxuriously creamy. Moderate negative space surrounds the pasta mound, ensuring the dish is the clear focal point. The plate rests on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are arranged beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a casual restaurant atmosphere, with natural, even lighting illuminating the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Chardonnay.

ingredients.name: Mixed wild mushrooms (e.g., cremini, shiitake, oyster)

instructions: Rehydrate dried porcini mushrooms in 150ml hot water for 20 minutes. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, reserving it. Coarsely chop rehydrated porcini.

Heat olive oil and butter in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add sliced and torn fresh wild mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are golden brown and their moisture has evaporated, about 8-10 minutes. Remove cooked mushrooms from the pan and set aside.
Add diced shallots to the same pan. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped rehydrated porcini. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Pour in reserved porcini liquid and vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes to slightly reduce the sauce.
Return the cooked fresh mushrooms to the pan. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 2-3 minutes until the sauce slightly thickens. Season the ragu generously with salt and black pepper.
Meanwhile, cook pappardelle in a large pot of generously salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Before draining, reserve 200ml of the pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add the cooked pappardelle directly to the mushroom ragu in the pan. Add half of the grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and half of the chopped fresh parsley.

Toss the pasta vigorously to coat it evenly with the sauce. Add reserved pasta water gradually, a tablespoon at a time, until the sauce emulsifies and beautifully coats every strand of pasta. The sauce should be creamy and cling to the pasta.
Serve immediately in warm bowls, garnished with the remaining Parmigiano-Reggiano and fresh parsley.
notes: For best flavor, use a variety of fresh wild mushrooms. Dried porcini add deep umami notes.
Adjust the amount of pasta water to achieve your desired sauce consistency; it should be fluid and coat the pasta well.
traditional_techniques: Sautéing mushrooms to achieve deep browning and flavor development (Maillard reaction)
Deglazing the pan to capture browned bits and build flavor
Emulsifying pasta with sauce and starchy pasta water for a cohesive, creamy texture

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Green Lentils with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of braised green lentils forms a rustic mound at the center of a clean, white porcelain plate. The lentils are plump, tender, and retain their shape, showing a rich, earthy green-brown hue. Scattered artfully around and nestled among the lentils are chunky, roasted root vegetables. Vibrant orange carrot and sweet potato chunks, pale yellow parsnip coins, and deep purple beetroot wedges display slightly caramelized edges, indicating a tender, roasted texture. A bright green sprinkle of fresh lemon-herb gremolata adorns the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface with a natural, even light. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate, completing the casual dining setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Rinse lentils thoroughly. Set aside.
Peel and dice onion, carrots, and celery for lentils into small cubes. Mince 2 garlic cloves.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.

Add rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 30-35 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Stir occasionally. Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
While lentils cook, peel root vegetables. Cut carrots and parsnips into thick coins or rustic chunks. Cut sweet potato into 2 cm cubes. Cut beetroot into wedges.
Toss cut root vegetables with 45 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a large baking sheet. Spread in a single layer.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Flip halfway through.
For gremolata: Finely chop fresh parsley. Zest the lemon. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Combine parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic in a small bowl.
Taste and adjust seasoning for lentils. Add salt and pepper as needed.

To serve: Spoon a generous portion of braised lentils onto each plate. Arrange roasted root vegetables artistically around and on top of the lentils. Sprinkle generously with gremolata. Serve immediately.
notes: For a richer flavor, a splash of red wine can be added to the lentils after sautéing the tomato paste, before adding broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Parmesan Cream Sauce and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, creamy Parmesan sauce is generously spooned over the chicken, cascading slightly onto the plate. Alongside, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets are neatly arranged, their edges showing a slight char from roasting. The dish presents a balanced composition of colors: the deep golden chicken, the bright green broccoli, and the creamy white sauce, all flecked with fresh green chopped parsley. The textures are apparent: crispy-edged chicken, tender-crisp broccoli, and a smooth, luxurious sauce. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, creating a professional yet approachable modern bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet, coating them with the sauce.
Serve immediately. Plate one chicken breast with a generous portion of Parmesan cream sauce. Arrange roasted broccoli florets alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Adjust sauce thickness by simmering longer or adding a small amount of extra broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Fermented Broth with Plant-Based Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of clear, amber broth fills a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic bowl. Substantial chunks of golden-brown plant-based 'chicken' are nestled within the broth. Precisely diced orange carrots and parsnips, along with thin, wavy slices of rehydrated shiitake mushrooms, are distributed throughout the soup. A vibrant scattering of blanched leafy green tops provides a fresh, verdant contrast on the surface. The broth glistens lightly, showcasing its depth. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood table. A simple, undyed linen napkin is folded beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the organic textures of the food and setting. The background is clean and minimalist, hinting at natural elements. The plating is uncrowded, with ample negative space around the bowl.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (onion skins, carrot peels, celery ends)
Fermented vegetable brine (e.g., kimchi liquid or sauerkraut juice)
Fresh leafy greens (e.g., radish greens, carrot tops, spinach)

instructions: Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms in 500 ml hot water for 30 minutes. Reserve mushroom liquid. Thinly slice rehydrated mushrooms.

Prepare vegetable broth: Combine vegetable scraps, peeled ginger (reserve ginger skin), and garlic cloves (unpeeled) in a large pot. Add kombu. Pour in 2 liters cold water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 45 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids. This is your zero-waste broth base.
Peel carrots and parsnips. Reserve peels for next broth batch. Dice carrots and parsnips into 1 cm cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add plant-based chicken pieces. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove from pot. Set aside.
Add diced carrots, parsnips, and sliced rehydrated mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in the prepared zero-waste broth and reserved mushroom liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook vegetables until tender-crisp, about 10-12 minutes.
Stir in fermented vegetable brine and soy sauce. Add seared plant-based chicken pieces. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Blanch fresh leafy greens in a separate pot of boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain immediately. This uses edible parts often discarded.
Season soup with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with blanched leafy greens.
notes: Save all vegetable scraps, herb stems, and onion skins for future broth making.
Fermented vegetable brine adds a complex, savory depth and probiotic benefits.
Adjust the amount of fermented brine to your preference for tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, alongside a mound of fluffy white jasmine rice. The chicken mince, cooked to a rich brown, is mixed with vibrant green wilted basil leaves and flecks of red chili. A perfectly fried egg with a crisp edge and a glossy, runny yolk rests atop the rice. The dish displays a balanced composition of textures and colors: the tender chicken, fresh basil, and the golden egg. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing each element to stand out. A set of chopsticks rests beside the plate, on a simple wooden table, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting with an authentic Thai culinary touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) for extra seasoning.
Traditionally eaten with jasmine rice as a staple accompaniment.
A fried egg (kai dao) is a common and essential topping.
instructions: Prepare the sauce: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Mix well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat until smoking.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken mince to the wok. Break up the chicken with a spatula. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Pour the prepared sauce over the chicken. Stir quickly to coat all ingredients.
Add the basil leaves. Stir-fry for 30-60 seconds until basil wilts but retains vibrant green color.
Remove from heat immediately.
While chicken cooks, fry 4 eggs sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Serve the Thai Basil Chicken stir-fry immediately over individual portions of cooked jasmine rice, topped with a fried egg.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Sausage and Potato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hearty Sausage and Potato Skillet presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a worn wooden dining table. The dish features a rich, creamy, reddish-orange tomato sauce enveloping browned, 2cm diced potatoes and crumbled, cooked sausage. Melted white cheddar cheese threads through the sauce, creating a comforting texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the top. A thick slice of crusty, golden-brown bread rests casually beside the bowl, ready for dipping. A small, simple white bowl holds a refreshing side salad of thinly sliced green cucumber and pale gherkins. The setting is a cozy, homely family kitchen with warm, natural lighting. The overall arrangement is natural and unpretentious.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style directly from the skillet or in individual bowls.
Provide crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
instructions: Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain well.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add drained potatoes. Cook until golden brown and tender, about 10-12 minutes. Remove potatoes. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add sausage. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat. Remove sausage. Set aside.
Add butter to the skillet. Finely dice onion. Add to skillet. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in milk. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Return cooked sausage and potatoes to the skillet. Stir to combine with the sauce.
Grate cheddar cheese. Stir into the skillet until melted and the sauce is creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
For the salad: Thinly slice cucumber and gherkins. Combine in a small bowl. Dress with white vinegar, a pinch of salt, and chopped fresh dill.
notes: This dish is excellent for a comforting family meal.
Adjust seasoning to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Buckwheat Tofu Waffles with Roasted Radish
recipes.special_requests: plant-based, waffles, 180g of tofu, all ingredients inside, no sugar, seasonings, no sauces
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown Fermented Buckwheat Tofu Waffles rests on a round, natural beige ceramic plate. The waffles exhibit a crisp, textured exterior from the waffle iron, with a soft, airy interior. Scattered around and atop the waffles are roasted radish wedges, their vibrant pink and red hues deepened by caramelization, showcasing their tender-crisp texture. The arrangement is clean and natural, allowing ample negative space on the plate. The entire composition is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its earthy colors and simple elegance, highlighting a sustainable, ingredient-focused approach.
instructions: Rinse buckwheat groats thoroughly. Place groats in a bowl with 150ml water. Cover loosely and let ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours.

Drain fermented buckwheat groats, reserving 15ml of the soaking liquid. Combine drained groats with pressed tofu in a blender. Blend until smooth. Add salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust batter consistency with reserved soaking liquid if too thick.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash radishes. Cut radishes into wedges. Toss radish wedges with 5ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Spread radishes in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast radishes for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and lightly caramelized.

Preheat waffle iron. Lightly brush waffle iron plates with remaining 10ml olive oil. Pour enough batter to cover the waffle plate. Cook until waffles are golden brown and crisp. Repeat with remaining batter.
Plate the cooked waffles. Top generously with the roasted radish wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lacto-Fermented Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, rests whole on a round, unglazed ceramic plate in creamy off-white. Adjacent, a vibrant medley of lacto-fermented root vegetables—carrots, parsnips, and daikon radish—are artfully arranged. These vegetables, cut into irregular batons and wedges, display natural shapes and slightly translucent textures, with earthy orange and pale cream tones. A light, herb-infused pan sauce is delicately drizzled around the chicken. The dish is minimally garnished with a fresh thyme sprig and a few thinly sliced pickled radish rounds for crimson contrast. The clean composition features generous negative space, highlighting the natural beauty and sustainable ethos. It sits on a light, natural wood surface with an undyed linen napkin.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add rosemary, thyme, and smashed garlic cloves to skillet.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven at 200°C (390°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Add 100ml water to deglaze, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly. This is the pan sauce.
Gently warm the lacto-fermented root vegetables in a separate pan or serve at room temperature.
Plate one chicken thigh per serving. Arrange a portion of fermented root vegetables alongside.
Drizzle chicken and vegetables with the pan sauce. Serve immediately.
notes: To prepare lacto-fermented root vegetables: Combine 500g peeled, cut root vegetables (carrots, daikon, parsnips) with a brine of 500ml non-chlorinated water and 15g sea salt. Pack tightly into a clean glass jar, ensuring vegetables are submerged. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, then refrigerate.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chocolate Sourdough Brownies with Berry Preserve
recipes.visual_description: A single, rich dark brown square brownie with a slightly crinkled top is centered on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The brownie is a thick square, showing its dense, moist interior. Adjacent to the brownie, a vibrant dollop of ruby-red berry preserve glistens, its texture showing the natural seeds of the berries. The presentation is minimalistic, emphasizing the natural beauty and contrasting colors of the dark chocolate and bright berries. There is ample white space around the food. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is gently folded beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle hint of green foliage from a potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. A simple, unadorned fork or spoon lies beside the plate, ready for dessert.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil (e.g., sunflower or melted coconut oil)

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking pan with parchment paper.
Melt dark chocolate using a double boiler or microwave. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk together sourdough discard, coconut sugar, oil, plant-based milk, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Stir in the melted chocolate until smooth.
In a separate bowl, combine cacao powder, flour, baking powder, and sea salt.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared baking pan. Spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. A toothpick inserted should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
While brownies bake, prepare the berry preserve. In a small saucepan, combine mixed berries, maple syrup, and lemon zest.
Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, mashing berries occasionally, until softened and slightly thickened.
Stir in chia seeds. Remove from heat. Let cool. The preserve will thicken as it cools.
Remove brownies from oven. Let cool completely in the pan before lifting out and cutting into 9 squares.
Serve each brownie square with a generous dollop of berry preserve.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh with crisp, golden-brown skin rests atop a generous bed of deeply caramelized, amber-hued onion slices. The chicken is tender, showing its natural form, not sliced. A rich, savory pan sauce, slightly thickened, coats the chicken and onions, reflecting light. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a vibrant contrast. The plate is a rustic, off-white ceramic, placed on a warm, well-used wooden kitchen table. A simple fork and knife are set beside it. The background is a soft-focus, lived-in kitchen atmosphere with warm lighting. The overall impression is comforting and hearty.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes to soak up the sauce
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter to the pot. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until onions are deeply caramelized and very soft.
Add minced garlic, bay leaf, and fresh thyme leaves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure liquid comes halfway up the chicken.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and is very tender.
Remove lid. Discard bay leaf. If sauce is too thin, increase heat to medium. Simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This dish can be prepared a day in advance and reheated gently for enhanced flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Mushroom and Rice Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing a medley of textures and natural colors. Warm, slightly cooled white rice forms a base, loosely mixed with tender, golden-brown sautéed mushroom slices. Vibrant halved cherry tomatoes and crisp, diced cucumber add pops of red and green. Thinly sliced red onion provides a subtle purple contrast. Finely diced red chilies are scattered throughout, hinting at a gentle warmth. A light vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, enhancing their natural sheen. The arrangement is casual and abundant, with ingredients touching and overlapping, reflecting a homely, comforting meal. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, warm kitchen light. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed nearby, completing the unpretentious, family-style presentation.
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside to cool slightly.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms from pan.
Add another 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Add minced garlic and diced red chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Return cooked mushrooms to the pan with garlic and chili. Stir to combine. Remove from heat.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, and honey (if using). Season with salt and black pepper.
In a large serving bowl, combine cooked rice, sautéed mushroom mixture, mixed salad greens, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss until all components are evenly coated.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Baked Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Lemon Herb Baked Chicken and Potatoes rests casually on an everyday ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The plate holds two golden-brown, baked chicken thighs, showing their natural shape and slightly crisp skin. Alongside are tender, roasted potato wedges, some with caramelized edges, and soft, sweet onion wedges. The colors are warm and inviting: golden chicken and potatoes, pale yellow lemon slices, and flecks of green from the herbs. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, unpretentious appearance. A few fresh parsley leaves are scattered over the dish for a touch of vibrant green. The setting includes simple, silver flatware and a casually folded cloth napkin, bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, emphasizing a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot directly from the baking sheet or plated individually.
Pair with a simple green salad for a balanced meal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Red Bliss)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm wedges. Cut onion into thick wedges. Mince garlic.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, and minced garlic.
Add 30ml olive oil, chopped rosemary leaves, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Pat chicken thighs dry. In the same bowl, toss chicken with remaining 30ml olive oil, half the lemon juiced, salt, and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs among the vegetables on the baking sheet. Thinly slice the other half of the lemon and place slices over chicken and vegetables.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Flip chicken and vegetables. Pour chicken broth over ingredients if desired.
Continue baking for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef and Mushroom Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Savory Beef and Mushroom Stir-fry is presented in a simple, deep white ceramic bowl, nestled on a well-used wooden dining table. The bowl is filled with fluffy white steamed long-grain rice, generously topped with glossy, dark brown beef chunks and earthy, sautéed mushroom slices. The beef is tender and glistening with sauce, while the mushrooms show slight caramelization. Bright green sliced green onions are scattered casually over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. A pair of wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a simple cloth napkin. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen with warm, natural lighting. The overall presentation is comforting and approachable, highlighting the hearty, home-cooked nature of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
Offer chili oil or sriracha on the side for added heat.
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Slice beef against the grain into thin strips or bite-sized chunks.
In a bowl, combine 30ml soy sauce, 5ml sesame oil, and 5g cornstarch. Add beef. Toss to coat. Marinate 15 minutes.
Slice mushrooms. Mince ginger and garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30ml soy sauce, 10ml sesame oil, 10g cornstarch, and beef broth. Set aside.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over high heat.
Add marinated beef. Stir-fry 2-3 minutes until browned. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove beef from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the pan.
Add mushrooms. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Add minced ginger and garlic to the pan. Stir-fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Return cooked beef to the pan. Stir the sauce mixture again. Pour sauce over beef and vegetables.
Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve immediately over hot steamed rice. Garnish with sliced green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Cabbage & Root Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, skin-on, sits prominently on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The chicken skin is a rich, deep golden-brown and visibly crispy, while the meat appears juicy. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat, slightly mounded portion of quick-fermented green cabbage presents a pale, vibrant green hue with a tender, slightly translucent texture. Scattered around the main components are thin, irregular, golden-brown root vegetable crisps, showcasing their brittle, airy texture. The plating is minimalistic, with ample white space on the plate, emphasizing the natural beauty and distinct textures of each ingredient. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. The table surface is light, natural bamboo or reclaimed wood. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of blurred green foliage, suggesting an eco-conscious and natural setting. The overall presentation is simple, clean, and highlights the sustainable elements of the dish.

ingredients.name: Fine sea salt
ingredients.quantity: 15 g (for cabbage), plus more for seasoning

instructions: Prepare fermented cabbage: Remove outer leaves from cabbage. Shred remaining cabbage thinly. Place shredded cabbage in a large bowl. Add 15 g fine sea salt. Massage cabbage vigorously with hands for 5-7 minutes until it softens and releases liquid.

Pack massaged cabbage tightly into a clean 1-liter glass jar. Pour released liquid over cabbage. If liquid does not cover cabbage, add filtered water until cabbage is fully submerged. Ensure no cabbage bits float. Seal jar. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare root crisps: Wash carrots and parsnips thoroughly. Use a vegetable peeler to create long, thin strips of peels. Discard any remaining root cores or save for stock. In a bowl, toss peels with 15 ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread peels in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Bake root crisps for 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove from oven and cool on a wire rack.
Cook chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden brown and crispy. Do not move chicken during this time.
Flip chicken thighs. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from oven and let rest for 5 minutes.

To serve: Place one seared chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of fermented cabbage beside the chicken. Artfully arrange a scattering of crispy root vegetable peels around the dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Cherry Tomato and Thyme Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Cherry Tomato and Thyme Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The soup has a rich, deep red color and a smooth, velvety texture. It fills the bowl generously, leaving appropriate negative space around the rim. A small, vibrant sprig of fresh thyme is placed gently on the soup's surface as a simple, functional garnish. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showcasing its natural grain. A casually folded, off-white cloth napkin is placed beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere. The focus is entirely on the inviting, homely soup.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Combine pitted cherries, cherry tomatoes, roughly chopped red onion, and unpeeled garlic cloves on a large baking tray.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast for 30-35 minutes. Vegetables should be soft and slightly caramelized.
Remove garlic from skins. Discard thyme sprigs.
Transfer roasted vegetables and cherries to a large pot.
Pour in vegetable stock. Add balsamic vinegar if using.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 10 minutes.
Use an immersion blender to blend soup until smooth. Alternatively, blend in batches in a regular blender.
Adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Buckwheat Waffles with Fermented Tofu and Radish Green Pesto
recipes.special_requests: plant-based, waffles, 180g of tofu, all ingredients inside, no sugar, seasonings
recipes.visual_description: A single savory buckwheat waffle, golden-brown with crisp edges, rests centrally on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate. A few thick, seared tofu cubes, displaying a subtle golden crust from cooking, are arranged naturally on one side of the waffle. Thin, vibrant pink radish rounds are artfully scattered, creating a fresh contrast. A small dollop of deep green radish green pesto is placed beside the waffle, adding a rich color accent. The plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The table surface is light, natural wood or stone. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly visible. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting textures and colors. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of a green plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. The overall presentation is clean, simple, and showcases the inherent beauty of each ingredient.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a standalone main course.
Pair with a simple fermented vegetable side, such as quick-pickled cucumber or sauerkraut.
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut pressed tofu into 2 cm thick cubes.
Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, and miso paste in a bowl. Add tofu cubes. Gently toss to coat. Marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Wash radishes and separate greens. Thinly slice radishes into rounds. Set aside.

For the pesto, combine radish greens, 20 ml olive oil, peeled garlic clove, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a small food processor. Blend until smooth. Add a splash of water if needed to reach desired consistency.
In a separate bowl, whisk together buckwheat flour, baking powder, and 2g salt. Gradually add water or plant milk, whisking until a smooth batter forms. Do not overmix.
Preheat waffle iron. Lightly grease if necessary. Pour enough batter for one waffle. Cook according to waffle iron instructions until golden brown and crisp.
Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add marinated tofu cubes. Cook for 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden and slightly crispy.

Place the cooked buckwheat waffle on a plate. Arrange seared tofu cubes on top. Scatter thin radish rounds around the tofu. Spoon radish green pesto alongside or over the tofu and waffle. Serve immediately.
notes: Pressing tofu is crucial for texture and flavor absorption.
Adjust pesto consistency by adding more water or olive oil.
This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing radish greens.
traditional_techniques: Fermentation (implied in miso and soy sauce, quick pickling for radish)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chocolate-Strawberry Glazed Pork Tenderloin
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-brown seared pork tenderloin medallions rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork, cut into thick, succulent rounds, is glistening, generously coated with a rich, glossy dark chocolate-strawberry glaze. The deep reddish-brown sauce has subtle hints of strawberry and a smooth, thick texture. Freshly chopped bright green chives are scattered over the pork, providing a vibrant color contrast. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a gently blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat pork tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork tenderloin on all sides until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes total.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove pork from skillet, rest on a cutting board, tent with foil.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add shallot and minced garlic to skillet. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in apple cider vinegar. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken broth, hot sauce, and quartered strawberries to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until strawberries soften.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in chopped dark chocolate and butter until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested pork tenderloin into thick medallions, approximately 2.5 cm thick.
Arrange pork medallions on serving plates. Spoon generous amount of warm glaze over pork.
Garnish with fresh chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.
Ensure pork reaches 63°C for medium-rare; it will continue cooking while resting.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Apple & Onion Tarte Tatin with Crispy Chicken Skin Brittle
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly cut triangular slice of Caramelized Apple & Onion Tarte Tatin rests on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. The tarte features deeply caramelized, tender apple wedges and translucent, sweet onion rings, gleaming with a rich amber hue from the caramel, topped by a golden-brown, flaky puff pastry crust. Around the base of the tart slice, small, irregular shards of glossy, golden-amber crispy chicken skin brittle are artfully scattered, adding a unique textural and visual contrast. A very light dusting of white icing sugar delicately graces the top of the tarte. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and professional, showcasing the distinct textures and warm colors of the dessert. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table surface, a single silver dessert fork placed beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred restaurant-style background maintaining a casual yet refined atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream or a dollop of crème fraîche to complement the sweetness and provide a creamy contrast.

ingredients.name: Apples (firm, sweet-tart like Honeycrisp or Granny Smith)
Sweet onions (e.g., Vidalia or Walla Walla)
Chicken skin (from breast or thigh, trimmed of all fat)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).

Prepare chicken skin brittle: Lay chicken skin flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until very crispy and golden brown. Drain excess fat. Break into small, irregular shards. In a small saucepan, combine 30g granulated sugar with 15ml water. Heat until sugar dissolves and turns light amber caramel. Toss crispy chicken skin shards in caramel. Spread on parchment paper to cool and harden. Break into smaller brittle pieces.
Prepare fruit and onions: Peel, core, and cut apples into 1.5 cm thick wedges. Slice onions into thin rings.

Make caramel base: In a 24 cm oven-safe, heavy-bottomed skillet (preferably cast iron), melt 80g butter over medium heat. Add 120g granulated sugar and 15ml water. Cook without stirring until sugar melts and turns deep amber caramel. Remove from heat.
Arrange apples and onions: Carefully arrange apple wedges and onion rings tightly in concentric circles over the caramel in the skillet. Fill gaps as much as possible.
Add salt: Sprinkle a pinch of salt over the fruit and onions.
Top with pastry: Place the puff pastry sheet over the apples and onions, tucking the edges down around the fruit inside the skillet.
Bake tarte: Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and puffed.
Cool slightly: Remove from oven. Let cool in the skillet for 5-10 minutes. This helps the caramel set slightly and prevents sticking.
Invert tarte: Place a large serving plate over the skillet. Carefully and confidently invert the skillet onto the plate. Lift the skillet slowly.
Serve: Dust lightly with icing sugar. Scatter crispy chicken skin brittle around the tarte slices. Serve warm.
notes: Ensure chicken skin is trimmed of all fat for the best brittle texture and flavor.
Be careful when making caramel; it is very hot.
The combination of apple and onion creates a unique sweet-savory depth that balances the dessert.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Rice Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The golden-yellow broth is clear, with visible steam rising. Within the broth are hearty, irregular chunks of cooked chicken, approximately 2cm cubes. Soft, fluffy white rice grains are suspended throughout. Bright orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and translucent diced onions are interspersed, adding color and texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside it. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen at home.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh

instructions: Dice chicken into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Dice carrots, celery, and onion. Add to the same pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Add rice. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender. Stir occasionally.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Confit Mille-Feuille with Smoked Salmon and Lemon-Dill Crème Fraîche
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve exquisitely crafted canapés presented on a polished white Carrara marble slab. Each canapé features a base of golden-brown, precisely cut rectangular potato confit, approximately 2cm by 4cm, showcasing its delicate, compressed layers. On top, a small, artfully placed dollop of creamy white lemon-dill crème fraîche, followed by a neatly folded, vibrant pink piece of premium smoked salmon. A single, perfectly placed bright green chive baton or a few glistening orange salmon roe pearls serve as the sole garnish, adding a pop of color and texture. Abundant white space surrounds each canapé, emphasizing their minimalist elegance and precise execution. The scene is bathed in dramatic, soft professional lighting, casting subtle shadows that highlight the textures and refined presentation. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, sits discreetly in the background on the marble surface.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Peel potatoes. Slice potatoes very thinly (1-2mm) using a mandoline.
Line a small, shallow terrine mold (approx. 10x15 cm) with parchment paper, leaving an overhang.
Layer potato slices tightly in the mold. Dot each layer with small pieces of butter. Season each layer lightly with salt and white pepper.
Repeat layering until all potatoes are used, pressing down firmly after each layer.
Cover the top with parchment paper. Place a weighted object (e.g., another pan with cans) on top to compress the potatoes.
Bake for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until potatoes are very tender when pierced.
Remove from oven. Increase weight on top. Chill in refrigerator overnight.
Carefully unmold the chilled potato terrine. Trim edges. Cut into precise rectangular canapé shapes (e.g., 2 cm x 4 cm). You should yield 8-12 pieces.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add a tiny bit of butter. Gently sear each potato piece until golden and crisp on all sides.
Finely chop fresh dill. Grate lemon zest from half a lemon.
In a small bowl, combine crème fraîche with chopped dill, lemon zest, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of white pepper. Mix well.
Cut smoked salmon into small, elegant pieces suitable for canapé topping.

To assemble: Place a seared potato confit base on your serving platter. Top with a small, artful dollop of lemon-dill crème fraîche. Carefully place a piece of smoked salmon on top of the crème fraîche.
Garnish each canapé with a single small chive baton or a few glistening salmon roe pearls.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Crab Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant mound of golden-brown rice sits centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Flakes of succulent, tender crab meat are visibly mixed throughout the rice, along with small, bright red diced tomatoes and translucent, diced white onion. Thin slices of vivid red chili are interspersed, providing bursts of color and a hint of heat. The texture is a harmonious mix of fluffy rice and tender ingredients. The dish is garnished generously with thinly sliced bright green spring onions and fresh cilantro leaves, scattered artfully over the top. A vibrant lime wedge is placed neatly on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, showcasing the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing colors. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate on a simple linen napkin, evoking a casual Asian dining experience under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for a bright citrus note.
Offer a side of sambal or chili oil for extra heat.
Traditionally enjoyed with a simple clear soup or sliced cucumber.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Add diced red onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add thinly sliced red chili and halved cherry tomatoes. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Push ingredients to one side of the wok. Pour beaten eggs into the empty side. Scramble until just set, then break into small pieces.
Add cooked brown rice to the wok. Break up any clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry vigorously for 3-4 minutes, ensuring rice is heated through.
In a small bowl, combine light soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and white pepper. Pour sauce mixture over the rice.
Continue to stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, ensuring rice is evenly coated and slightly caramelized.
Add picked crab meat to the wok. Gently toss for 1 minute to heat the crab through. Avoid overmixing.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with sesame oil. Toss gently.
Divide the fried rice among 4 serving plates. Garnish generously with thinly sliced spring onions and fresh cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.
notes: For best results, use day-old cooked brown rice. This prevents stickiness and allows for better stir-frying.
Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level. For milder heat, remove chili seeds.
traditional_techniques: Wok hei (achieving high-heat wok aroma and char)

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Gratin with Gruyere
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Gratin with Gruyere is presented in a classic white porcelain oval gratin dish, set on a simple light wooden table surface. The dish features tender, thinly sliced potatoes, layered and baked until soft, with a golden-brown, bubbly Gruyere cheese crust on top. Visible beneath the cheese are creamy, garlic-infused potato slices. Two generous, irregular chunks of seared chicken thigh, with a golden-brown exterior, are nestled amidst the gratin, not sliced or fanned. The rich, savory sauce is visible, coating the potatoes. Freshly chopped green parsley and a few small thyme leaves are scattered over the top as a vibrant garnish. The plate is well-proportioned with appropriate negative space. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver bistro flatware are placed beside the dish. The scene is lit by soft, natural, even light, creating a professional yet inviting restaurant-style ambiance with a subtle, blurred background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Melt butter in the same skillet. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in heavy cream and fresh thyme sprigs. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
While sauce simmers, peel potatoes. Slice potatoes thinly, about 2-3mm thick.
Grate Gruyere cheese.
Arrange a layer of sliced potatoes in the bottom of the skillet. Place seared chicken thighs over the potatoes. Top with another layer of potatoes.
Pour the sauce evenly over the potatoes and chicken.
Sprinkle grated Gruyere cheese generously over the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the cheese is bubbly and golden brown. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons nested in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Large, 3cm tender chunks of braised beef are distributed naturally throughout the pasta, coated in a thick, mahogany-colored tomato sauce. The sauce has a glossy sheen and visible small bits of diced carrots and onions. The dish is topped with a light, airy snowfall of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. A small pinch of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the center. The bowl sits on a rustic light-wood bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural daylight illuminates the textures of the shredded beef fibers and the silkiness of the pasta ribbons.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of full-bodied red wine like Chianti
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread for 'fare la scarpetta'
Present in wide-rimmed pasta bowls
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the same pot. Sauté 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and herb sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Remove herb sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Boil salted water in a large pot. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with the ragu and reserved water over low heat for 1 minute.
Serve immediately with grated cheese.
notes: Ensure the beef is seared deeply for maximum flavor development.
If the sauce is too thick, add more pasta water during the finishing stage.
Chuck roast or shin are the best cuts for this long-braising method.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Ragu with Rigatoni and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Rigatoni with Spicy Beef Ragu is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, centered on a natural wooden table surface. The al dente rigatoni noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, deep red ragu, showcasing tender, slow-cooked diced beef chunks. A luscious, thick texture defines the sauce, clinging well to every pasta piece. Patches of golden-brown, bubbly melted mozzarella cheese crown the top, with some delightful cheese strands stretching. Bright green fresh basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding a vibrant color contrast. A folded white cotton napkin and a traditional silver fork are placed beside the bowl. A small, rustic piece of crusty bread rests subtly nearby, completing the casual bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the ragu.
Offer grated Parmesan cheese on the side for individual preference.
instructions: Pat diced beef dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches until deeply colored on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, hot sauce, and oregano.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2-3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Preheat oven broiler. Stir cooked rigatoni into the beef ragu.
Transfer pasta and ragu to an oven-safe serving dish or individual gratin dishes. Tear or shred mozzarella over the top.
Broil for 3-5 minutes, or until mozzarella is melted and bubbly and lightly browned.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Taleggio Barley Risotto with Swiss Chard
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous portion of creamy barley risotto. The barley is cooked to a fluid, al dente consistency. Interspersed are tender, bite-sized chunks of pan-seared chicken, lightly browned. Vibrant green swiss chard leaves and finely chopped stems are folded in, adding color and subtle bitterness. Melted Taleggio cheese creates a luxurious, smooth texture, with occasional pockets of its characteristic orange rind visible. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted caraway seeds for aromatic crunch. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan and fresh parsley sprigs add freshness. The plating is clean, inviting, with moderate negative space, set on a simple wooden table with a white linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to sop up the creamy risotto.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine common to Northern Italy.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes in batches until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken and set aside.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Separate swiss chard leaves from stems. Chop stems into 1 cm pieces. Coarsely chop leaves.
Add remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and chard stems. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add pearl barley to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast lightly.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until liquid is almost fully absorbed.

Begin adding hot chicken broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently, waiting until each addition is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 30-40 minutes, until barley is creamy and al dente.
During the last 5 minutes of cooking, stir in chopped swiss chard leaves. Cook until wilted and tender.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in cooked chicken, remaining butter, and diced Taleggio cheese. Stir vigorously until cheese is melted and risotto is creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small dry pan, toast caraway seeds over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Do not burn.
Ladle the barley risotto into warm serving bowls. Garnish each serving with toasted caraway seeds, a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese, and fresh parsley sprigs. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust broth quantity for desired risotto consistency; some barley types absorb more liquid than others.
traditional_techniques: Risottatura (risotto cooking method applied to barley)

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Coq au Vin
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Coq au Vin on a round, clean white porcelain plate, presented on a simple wooden table. A rich, dark red wine sauce pools around a whole, golden-brown braised chicken leg quarter. Scattered around the chicken and lightly submerged in the sauce are earthy brown quartered cremini mushrooms, glistening white pearl onions, and vibrant orange 2cm carrot chunks. A delicate sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a touch of freshness. The textures are varied: tender chicken, soft vegetables, and a glossy, slightly thickened sauce. The background features a subtly out-of-focus modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware rest beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce
Simple green salad with a vinaigrette
Mashed potatoes or buttered noodles

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown, 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side, 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced bacon to Dutch oven. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon, reserve fat.
Add pearl onions to rendered bacon fat. Sauté until lightly browned, 5 minutes. Remove onions.
Add mushrooms to Dutch oven. Sauté until browned and tender, 7-10 minutes. Remove mushrooms.
Add carrots, celery, and minced garlic to Dutch oven. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Deglaze with brandy (if using). Scrape bottom of pot.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Cook 2 minutes, stirring.
Gradually pour in red wine and chicken stock, stirring constantly. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken, bacon, pearl onions, and mushrooms to Dutch oven. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and braise in oven at 160°C for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove chicken, bacon, onions, and mushrooms. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Skim excess fat from sauce. Reduce sauce on stovetop if desired, until slightly thickened.
Stir butter into sauce until melted and incorporated. Adjust seasoning.
Return chicken, bacon, onions, and mushrooms to sauce. Heat through.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Mushroom Chocolate Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast rests centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, with a golden-brown crust, is presented whole. A generous, glossy, dark brown sauce, rich with finely chopped dark chocolate and the subtle red hue of sriracha, cascades artfully over and around the chicken. Interspersed within the sauce are varied shapes of tender, sautéed mushrooms – some quartered, some sliced – adding earthy texture. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped cilantro provides a contrasting pop of green. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A neatly folded cotton napkin and minimal, modern flatware are positioned beside the plate, completing a refined yet approachable bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed rice or roasted seasonal vegetables.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in chopped dark chocolate and hot sauce until chocolate is melted and sauce is smooth.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer gently 2 minutes to warm through.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with fresh cilantro or parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Pickled Red Onion Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and naturally composed salad is presented on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a warm off-white tone. Diced roasted potatoes form a scattered base, exhibiting golden-brown edges. Blanched broccoli florets, deep green and tender-crisp, are artistically distributed among the potatoes. Sliced sautéed cremini mushrooms, rich brown and meaty, are interspersed throughout. Halved cherry tomatoes, displaying bright red hues, add pops of color and juicy texture. Thinly sliced, vibrant pink pickled red onion pieces are scattered, providing a striking visual contrast and a hint of tang. Crumbled vegan feta cheese, creamy white, is sprinkled over the entire dish. A light, glistening golden dressing is visibly drizzled, binding the elements. The plate is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simply folded, undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, with a minimalist background suggesting natural elements without distraction.
instructions: Prepare pickled red onion: Thinly slice the red onion. In a small saucepan, combine 60 ml apple cider vinegar, 120 ml water, 10 g sugar, and 5 g salt. Bring to a simmer until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot brine over sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 weeks.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, 2 g salt, and 2 g black pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly crisped.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Slice cremini mushrooms. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and sauté for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and tender. Season with a pinch of salt.
Halve cherry tomatoes.

Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 15 ml olive oil, remaining 60 ml apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, remaining 3 g salt, and remaining 3 g black pepper. Add 30 ml of the pickled red onion brine for extra flavor.
In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, blanched broccoli, sautéed mushrooms, halved cherry tomatoes, and desired amount of pickled red onion.
Crumble vegan feta cheese over the salad. Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish the salad with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Eggplant and Tomato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Smoked Paprika Eggplant and Tomato Stew fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Thick chunks of tender, dark purple eggplant are nestled among vibrant red crushed tomatoes and diced red bell pepper. The stew has a rich, earthy red-brown hue from the smoked paprika. Visible pieces of caramelized onion and minced garlic are present. The texture is thick and comforting, with the eggplant holding its shape but yielding easily. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table in a homely kitchen. A piece of crusty, artisanal bread rests casually beside the bowl. The setting is warm and inviting, with natural, soft lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve with a simple green salad
instructions: Cut eggplant into 3 cm cubes. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt. Let sit 30 minutes. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add eggplant. Cook until browned on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove eggplant. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil to the pot. Add chopped onion and diced red bell pepper. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked eggplant to the pot. Stir well. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until eggplant is very tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This stew deepens in flavor overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Seared Beef Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Potato and Seared Beef Salad is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Cubed tender potatoes, halved vibrant green beans, halved bright red cherry tomatoes, finely diced red onion, and crisp celery are loosely mixed, showcasing natural colors and textures. Small, irregular chunks of seared beef, with a rich brown crust, are nestled among the vegetables as a hearty protein. A creamy, pale yellow dressing lightly coats all components. Coarsely chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over, adding a pop of green. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a family kitchen. A casual cloth napkin and fork are beside it. Warm, soft light illuminates the dish, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere. The presentation is unpretentious, emphasizing wholesome comfort food.
instructions: Wash and cube potatoes into 2 cm pieces. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain and let cool slightly.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes. Immediately transfer to ice water to stop cooking. Drain and halve.
Pat beef dry. Cut into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks for 2-3 minutes per side until browned. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove from pan and let rest.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Finely dice red onion and celery.
Chop fresh parsley coarsely.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Add cooled potatoes, green beans, cherry tomatoes, diced red onion, diced celery, and seared beef chunks to the bowl with the dressing.
Gently fold all ingredients until well combined and coated with dressing. Stir in chopped parsley.
Serve immediately or chill for flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Tofu Buckwheat Waffles with Quick-Pickled Radish
recipes.visual_description: Two to three golden-brown savory buckwheat waffles, slightly overlapping, are centered on a matte cream ceramic plate. Thinly sliced, vibrant pink-red quick-pickled radish slices are artfully scattered over and around the waffles, their edges subtly curled. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh radish greens adds a contrasting pop of deep green. The crisp waffle exterior contrasts with the tender interior, complemented by the crunchy, tangy radish. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from above, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of a leafy green plant, ensuring the focus remains on the food.
instructions: Press tofu for 15 minutes to remove excess water. Crumble tofu into a bowl.

Add buckwheat flour, baking powder, salt, pepper, minced garlic, and nutritional yeast (if using) to crumbled tofu. Gradually whisk in water or plant milk and 5 ml olive oil until a thick, smooth batter forms. Do not overmix.
Preheat waffle iron. Brush with remaining olive oil. Pour batter into iron. Cook until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes.

Thinly slice radishes using a mandoline or sharp knife. In a small bowl, combine apple cider vinegar, 30 ml water, and sugar (if using). Add sliced radishes. Let sit for at least 10 minutes to quick pickle.
Finely chop radish greens (if using).
Place cooked waffles on a plate. Drain pickled radishes and arrange them over and around the waffles. Garnish with chopped radish greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato & Cucumber Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Tomato & Cucumber Rice Salad is presented in a generous, natural mound on a simple, round ceramic plate, showcasing its vibrant, fresh ingredients. Fluffy white rice forms the base, interspersed with vivid red diced tomatoes, bright green diced cucumber, crisp green bell pepper, and delicate purple flecks of finely diced red onion. Abundant chopped fresh parsley adds a contrasting deep green hue and herbaceous texture throughout. Golden, irregularly shaped rustic bread croutons are scattered generously on top and mixed within, providing a pleasing crunch and visual interest. A light sheen from the olive oil dressing coats the ingredients, highlighting their natural colors. The dish is arranged casually, as if served at a family meal, with some ingredients gently overlapping. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple cloth napkin and a standard fork, emphasizing a homely, comforting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of grilled halloumi cheese.
Offer with warm pita bread for scooping.
Pair with a light, chilled white wine.
instructions: Prepare croutons. Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss bread cubes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Bake croutons for 10-12 minutes, until golden and crisp. Let cool.
In a large bowl, combine cooled cooked rice, diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, finely diced red onion, diced green bell pepper, and chopped parsley.
Prepare dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml olive oil, lemon juice, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Pour dressing over the rice and vegetable mixture. Toss gently to combine all ingredients thoroughly.
Add the cooled croutons to the salad just before serving. Toss lightly. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Potato & Onion with Savory Lentil Crumble and Fermented Broth
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist and earthy presentation showcasing roasted potato chunks and caramelized onion wedges as the centerpiece. The potatoes are golden-brown with slightly crispy edges, cut into irregular, thick chunks. The onions are soft, translucent, and deeply caramelized to a rich brown. A generous scattering of savory lentil crumble, made from finely textured Puy lentils, nutritional yeast, and fresh herbs, rests atop and around the roasted vegetables, adding a subtle green and light brown contrast. A small, clear pool of warm, fermented onion broth, hinting at a delicate amber hue, encircles the base of the ingredients, providing a subtle sheen. The dish is served on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, highlighting the organic colors and textures. The composition is clean and uncluttered, with ample white space, emphasizing the natural beauty of each ingredient. A few fresh chive pieces are scattered over for a vibrant green accent. The setting is a light, natural wood or stone surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in a neutral beige.
