Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the dish's inviting warmth and texture, with a clean, uncluttered background featuring subtle natural elements.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, medium, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Yellow Onions
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Prepare Fermented Onion Broth Base: Combine thinly sliced red onion, apple cider vinegar, and water in a clean jar. Seal tightly. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly fizzy and tangy. Strain liquid, reserving fermented onions for other use.

Roast Potatoes and Onions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato chunks and yellow onion wedges with 30 ml olive oil, 2 sprigs thyme, 1 sprig rosemary, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 35-45 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.
Cook Lentils: In a small pot, combine rinsed Puy lentils with 400 ml vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until tender. Drain excess liquid if any.

Make Savory Lentil Crumble: In a pan, heat 15 ml olive oil. Add smashed garlic and cook until fragrant (1 minute). Add cooked lentils, remaining thyme and rosemary leaves (chopped finely), nutritional yeast, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Sauté gently for 5-7 minutes until slightly crisped.
Prepare Fermented Broth: In a small saucepan, combine 100 ml strained fermented onion broth base with 100 ml vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Keep warm.

Plate and Serve: Arrange roasted potato and onion chunks centrally on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of savory lentil crumble over and around the roasted vegetables. Pour a small pool of the warm fermented broth around the base of the dish. Garnish with fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Beef & Tomato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Rustic Beef & Tomato Stew fills a deep, slightly imperfect rustic ceramic bowl. Thick, seared beef chunks, roughly chopped softened onions, and bright red tomato pieces are generously nestled in a rich, reddish-brown gravy. The beef shows a deep caramelized crust, while the stew's natural colors are prominent. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a functional garnish. The bowl is placed on a well-used, light wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually draped beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, creating a cozy atmosphere. The plating is natural and unforced, with components overlapping comfortably, filling the plate without overcrowding. A sturdy, everyday metal spoon rests on the table, completing the unpretentious, comforting scene.
instructions: Cut beef into 3-4 cm chunks. Pat beef dry with paper towels. Toss beef with flour, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Roughly chop onions. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs before serving.
Chop fresh parsley for garnish. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Crab Risotto with Lemon and Saffron
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy, saffron-infused Crab Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale golden-yellow, maintains a fluid, natural consistency, pooling gently within the bowl. Visible throughout are delicate, tender chunks of white-pink crab meat, gently folded in, showcasing its pristine quality. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley crowns the dish, adding a pop of green. A thin, bright yellow lemon wheel or a twist of lemon peel is placed artfully on the rim. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a silver fork and spoon placed on a folded cotton napkin beside the bowl, set against a softly blurred, modern bistro background with natural, even lighting. The presentation is clean, professional, and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a 'primo piatto' (first course) or a light main course.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Warm stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Heat olive oil and 20 g butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add finely diced shallots. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent. Do not brown.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Add one ladleful of warm stock. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding stock, one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes 18-20 minutes.
Dissolve saffron threads in a small amount of warm stock. Add to risotto halfway through cooking.
Risotto should be creamy and al dente. It should flow slightly when the pan is tilted.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 40 g butter, grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Gently fold in crab meat. Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste.
Cover the pan and let risotto rest for 2 minutes.
Ladle risotto into warm bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Use high-quality fresh lump crab meat for the best flavor and texture.
Do not overcook the crab; it should be added at the very end and gently folded in to maintain its delicate texture.
Risotto should be 'all'onda' (wavy) in consistency, not stiff or dry.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (creaming the risotto with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and White Bean Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Roasted Tomato and White Bean Pasta Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of colors and textures. Tender farfalle pasta, light ivory in hue, forms the base. Scattered throughout are vibrant red roasted cherry tomato halves, some slightly blistered, alongside creamy white cannellini beans. Small, neatly diced cubes of cooked chicken breast are interspersed, providing a lean protein element. Halved fresh mozzarella bocconcini add soft white contrasts. Fresh, dark green baby arugula leaves are gently folded in, adding a pop of color and freshness. The salad is lightly coated with a glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette, visible on the pasta and vegetables. The composition is balanced, with ingredients artfully distributed but not overly arranged, allowing for moderate negative space. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate on a simple wooden table surface, under natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss halved cherry tomatoes with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and blistered.
Cook farfalle pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to cool.

While pasta cooks, season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Heat 10 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest, then dice into 2 cm cubes.
For the vinaigrette, whisk together extra virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, chopped basil, chopped oregano, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled pasta, roasted cherry tomatoes, drained cannellini beans, diced chicken, and halved mozzarella balls.
Pour vinaigrette over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Fold in baby arugula just before serving.
notes: This salad is excellent served at room temperature or chilled.
For best flavor, let the salad sit for 15 minutes after dressing before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Garlic Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a golden-brown, crisp-skinned chicken thigh as the centerpiece. It rests beside a pile of golden-roasted baby potato wedges and tender, roasted whole garlic cloves. Vibrant red, burst cherry tomatoes and fresh green oregano leaves are scattered amongst the components, adding pops of color. A light, glistening pan sauce, infused with chicken broth and lemon, pools subtly around the base. Fresh chopped parsley is generously sprinkled over the dish. The plating is organized yet organic, allowing natural textures and colors to shine. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin and a fork and knife placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting warmth and rustic elegance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the pan juices
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash baby potatoes. Cut larger potatoes in half. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Add unpeeled garlic cloves to the potato tray. Roast for 20 minutes.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Carefully transfer chicken to the baking tray with potatoes and garlic.
Add cherry tomatoes and fresh oregano sprigs to the tray. Toss gently.
Roast for an additional 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender.
While chicken roasts, deglaze the skillet with chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Squeeze juice from half a lemon into the broth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Once cooked, let chicken rest on the tray for 5 minutes.
To serve, place a roasted chicken thigh on a plate. Arrange roasted potatoes, garlic, and cherry tomatoes alongside.
Spoon the pan sauce over the chicken and vegetables. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The garlic cloves become soft and sweet when roasted and can be squeezed out of their skins onto the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Tofu with Creamy Buckwheat and Roasted Radishes
recipes.visual_description: Plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, a generous mound of creamy, pale golden buckwheat forms the base. Two thick, golden-brown pan-seared tofu slabs, with a distinct crisp exterior, are positioned neatly atop the buckwheat. Scattered around the tofu and buckwheat are vibrant red and pink roasted radish halves and quarters, their edges slightly caramelized, adding pops of color. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh chives provides a delicate garnish. The arrangement is balanced and professional, allowing for moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish in a clean bistro-style setting.
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut pressed tofu into 8 thick slabs.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve or quarter radishes. Toss radishes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp.
While radishes roast, heat 15 ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add buckwheat groats to the saucepan. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in 250 ml vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding remaining broth, 125 ml at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. Cook until buckwheat is tender and creamy, about 20-25 minutes total.
Stir nutritional yeast, remaining 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper into the cooked buckwheat. Adjust consistency with more broth if needed.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear tofu slabs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp.
Plate creamy buckwheat. Top with two seared tofu slabs per serving. Arrange roasted radishes around the dish.
Garnish with chopped fresh chives. Squeeze lemon juice over the entire dish before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Onion Sauce and Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared chicken thigh rests centrally on a bed of al dente whole grain fusilli pasta. The chicken, with its golden-brown, crispy skin, is presented as a whole piece. Around the chicken, a rich, rustic tomato-onion sauce, made from slow-cooked diced tomatoes and caramelized onions, pools gently, showcasing its deep reddish-brown hue and a few visible herb flecks. Alongside, a vibrant quick-fermented red onion and tomato relish, with thinly sliced red onion rings and small tomato wedges, adds a bright pop of color and texture. A thin, irregular shard of golden-brown aged cheddar crisp leans artfully against the chicken, providing a textural contrast. The composition is clean and uncrowded, allowing each element to breathe. The dish is served on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually folded to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's natural colors and textures. A subtle, out-of-focus hint of green foliage from a potted plant is visible in the background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare Quick Fermented Relish: Dice 200g tomatoes and thinly slice half a red onion. Combine in a bowl with a pinch of salt and 15ml white wine vinegar. Let sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate for longer fermentation up to 2 days.

Prepare Cheddar Crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grate aged cheddar cheese onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, forming four thin circles (approx. 8cm diameter). Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Let cool and harden. Break into irregular shards.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, rest on a cutting board.

Prepare Sauce: While chicken bakes, finely chop remaining 300g tomatoes and remaining 1.5 red onions. Mince garlic. In the same skillet (after removing chicken), add remaining 15ml olive oil if needed. Add chopped onions and cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in Dijon mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add whole grain fusilli pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 50ml pasta water.

Combine and Serve: Add drained pasta to the tomato-onion sauce. Add reserved pasta water if needed to achieve desired consistency. Slice chicken thighs in half if desired, or keep whole. Plate a portion of pasta and sauce. Top with a seared chicken thigh. Spoon a generous amount of the Quick Fermented Relish alongside. Garnish with cheddar crisp shards and fresh parsley or basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tofu Teriyaki Donburi
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Tofu Teriyaki Donburi is presented in an everyday, deep ceramic donburi bowl. A generous bed of fluffy white Japanese short-grain rice fills the bottom. Golden-brown, pan-fried tofu cubes, generously coated in a glossy, dark amber teriyaki glaze, are casually arranged on top of the rice. The tofu pieces are whole, not sliced or fanned. Bright green, thinly sliced green onions are scattered across the top, alongside a sprinkle of pale, toasted sesame seeds, adding contrasting color and texture. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. Chopsticks are casually placed beside the bowl. The scene evokes a relaxed, homely family dining atmosphere with natural imperfections and minimal clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of miso soup
Offer a side of pickled ginger (gari)
Use chopsticks for eating
instructions: Press tofu: Drain tofu. Wrap in paper towels. Place between two plates. Weigh down top plate with heavy object for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Prepare rice: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice in a rice cooker or pot according to package directions.
Cut tofu: Cut pressed tofu into 2 cm cubes.
Make teriyaki sauce: Combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves.

Cook tofu: Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes. Cook, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden brown and slightly crispy. This takes 8-10 minutes.

Glaze tofu: Pour teriyaki sauce over tofu in the pan. Bring to a simmer. In a separate small bowl, mix cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water to create a slurry. Add slurry to simmering sauce, stirring constantly. Cook until sauce thickens and coats tofu.
Assemble: Divide cooked rice among four donburi bowls. Arrange glazed tofu cubes over rice.
Garnish: Sprinkle generously with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Beef Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spicy Korean Beef Rice Bowl is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. A generous bed of fluffy, steamed short-grain white rice forms the base. Piled on top are irregular, medium-sized chunks of savory, deeply browned beef, interspersed with tender, caramelized slivers of onion and minced garlic. The beef exhibits a slight char and glossy coating from the spicy sauce. Scattered across the top are vibrant red, thinly sliced rounds of fresh chili and bright green, thinly sliced green onions, providing pops of color and freshness. A sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds adds a subtle textural contrast. The dish is arranged organically, allowing the textures and colors of the ingredients to speak for themselves, with moderate negative space in the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Chopsticks rest beside the bowl, ready for use. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a minimal, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small side dishes (banchan) such as kimchi or pickled radish.
Offer a clear, light broth on the side.
Eat with chopsticks and a spoon for the rice.

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin or short rib meat

instructions: Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.

Combine soy sauce, gochujang, gochugaru, sesame oil, sugar or honey, grated ginger, and black pepper in a bowl. Add beef chunks. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat cooking oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat.
Add marinated beef to the hot skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beef is browned and slightly caramelized. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding.
Add sliced onion and minced garlic to the skillet with the beef. Stir-fry for another 5-7 minutes until onions are tender-crisp and beef is cooked through.
Divide cooked rice among four individual serving bowls.
Spoon the spicy beef and onion mixture over the rice in each bowl.
Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced fresh red chili, sliced green onions, and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: High-heat stir-frying for caramelization and texture

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Parmesan Risotto with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Mushroom and Parmesan Risotto is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, positioned on a simple wooden table surface. The risotto forms a fluid, organic mound, showcasing its rich, creamy texture and light golden color. Sliced, golden-brown sautéed mushrooms are visibly folded into the risotto and gently arranged on top. A perfectly poached egg, with its delicate white set and a hint of its golden yolk peeking through, rests centrally on the risotto. The dish is garnished with a light sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped vibrant green parsley. To the side, a small plate holds a piece of crusty ciabatta bread, accompanied by standard European flatware (fork and spoon) and a cotton napkin. The setting is a modern bistro, with natural, even lighting casting soft shadows and a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background, highlighting the authentic Italian presentation and the inviting warmth of the dish. The entire plate and surrounding elements are visible, with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Clean mushrooms. Slice larger mushrooms. Set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 10g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the saucepan. Stir for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add one ladle of warm stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed before adding more. This takes about 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and rice al dente.

While risotto cooks, heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a separate pan. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté over medium-high heat until golden brown and tender, about 7-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside a few slices for garnish.

When risotto is nearly done, bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar if desired. Carefully crack each egg into a small bowl, then gently slide into the simmering water. Poach eggs for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny.

Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 50g butter and 80g grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and risotto is creamy (mantecatura). Fold in most of the sautéed mushrooms.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

To serve, ladle a generous portion of creamy risotto into each warm bowl. Place one poached egg gently on top of each serving. Garnish with remaining sautéed mushroom slices, a sprinkle of fresh Parmesan, and chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beer-Braised Chicken with Tomato Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening, rests atop a vibrant mound of reddish-orange brown rice. The chicken is whole, tender, with visible crispy skin edges. The rice is fluffy, infused with tomato, and shows flecks of red and orange. A rich, savory, slightly thickened beer-tomato braising sauce pools around the chicken and rice. Freshly chopped green cilantro is scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A bright green lime wedge is placed beside the chicken. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side for dipping into the sauce.
Offer extra lime wedges.

ingredients.name: Chili (e.g., jalapeño or serrano), finely diced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced chili, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, cook brown rice. Rinse brown rice thoroughly.
In a medium saucepan, combine brown rice with 500ml water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Taste braising liquid for seasoning. Adjust salt and pepper as needed.
To serve, place a mound of tomato brown rice on each plate. Top with a braised chicken thigh. Spoon generous amount of braising liquid over chicken and rice.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Roasted Bell Pepper Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared salmon fillet, skin side up, is artfully placed slightly off-center on a bed of creamy, vibrant roasted bell pepper risotto. The salmon boasts a crispy, golden-brown skin and a moist, flaky interior. The risotto is fluid, not mounded, showcasing perfectly cooked Arborio grains intertwined with visible, small diced red and yellow bell peppers and subtle flecks of minced red chili. Fresh, finely chopped green parsley is lightly scattered over the salmon and risotto, adding a burst of color. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, allowing ample negative space. The composition is balanced and inviting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the rich colors and varied textures. A simple wooden table and a folded white cotton napkin complete the casual bistro setting.
instructions: Prep vegetables: Dice red and yellow bell peppers into 5mm cubes. Mince red chili. Finely chop shallots. Mince garlic.
Start risotto: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped shallots. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice to the saucepan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice edges become translucent.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add broth: Begin adding warm vegetable broth, 240ml at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each addition to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
Add bell peppers: During the last 5 minutes of risotto cooking, stir in the diced red and yellow bell peppers.

Finish risotto: Remove saucepan from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and cold butter cubes. Stir vigorously until butter is melted and risotto is creamy and fluid. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.

Cook salmon: While risotto cooks, pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.

Sear salmon: Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 5-6 minutes until skin is crispy and golden-brown. Flip the fillets. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until salmon is cooked through and flakes easily (internal temperature 60°C).

Plate: Spoon the creamy bell pepper risotto onto warm dinner plates. Carefully place one pan-seared salmon fillet on top of each risotto portion. Garnish generously with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Saltimbocca with Prosciutto and Sage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Saltimbocca is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pan-seared chicken breast is a golden-brown, topped with crisped prosciutto and vibrant green sage leaves, adhering perfectly. A rich, glossy pan sauce, amber-brown with hints of lemon, is generously spooned over and around the chicken, pooling elegantly on the plate. The chicken, pounded to a uniform thickness, shows its tender, cooked interior where a small cut reveals it. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table. Silver flatware is neatly arranged beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin adds a touch of refinement. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting the textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered pasta or roasted asparagus.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound lightly with a mallet to an even 1 cm thickness.
Lay 2 slices of prosciutto over each chicken breast. Place 4 sage leaves evenly on top of the prosciutto. Secure prosciutto and sage with toothpicks if needed.
Lightly dredge the chicken, prosciutto-side down, in plain flour. Shake off excess.
Heat olive oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken, prosciutto-side down, in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes until prosciutto is crispy and golden.
Flip chicken over. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Keep warm.
Deglaze pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in remaining butter. Squeeze in lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer until slightly reduced, about 2 minutes.
Remove toothpicks from chicken. Place chicken on plates. Spoon sauce over.
notes: Ensure chicken is pounded to an even thickness for even cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing. Cook in batches if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Salsa and Carrot Top Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown and whole, is placed on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Alongside, thick chunks of roasted carrots and parsnips show their caramelized edges and vibrant hues. A generous, vibrant red dollop of chunky fermented tomato salsa, flecked with cilantro and red onion, rests atop and beside the chicken, adding fresh tang. Bright green, smooth carrot top pesto is drizzled sparingly over the chicken and vegetables, creating clean lines. The minimalistic composition leaves ample negative space. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin is neatly folded nearby. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, enhancing textures and colors. The background is clean, with a subtle hint of green foliage, ensuring the entire plate is visible.

ingredients.name: medium carrots, scrubbed, cut into thick chunks or wedges
medium parsnips, scrubbed, cut into thick chunks or wedges

instructions: Combine diced tomatoes, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and 5g sea salt in a clean bowl. Mix well.
Pack mixture tightly into a clean glass jar. Press down to remove air bubbles. Ensure vegetables are submerged in their own liquid. Leave 2-3 cm headspace.

Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily if not using an airlock. Store in refrigerator once fermented.

Combine carrot tops, garlic, walnuts, 30ml olive oil, lemon juice, 2g sea salt, and 1g black pepper in a food processor. Blend until smooth. Add a tablespoon of water if needed for desired consistency. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. On a baking tray, toss carrot and parsnip chunks with 30ml olive oil, 3g sea salt, and 2g black pepper.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs in hot skillet.
Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C and chicken is golden brown. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
Place a portion of roasted vegetables on each plate. Arrange a seared chicken thigh alongside the vegetables.
Spoon a generous dollop of fermented tomato salsa over and beside the chicken. Drizzle carrot top pesto over the chicken and vegetables. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Warm Goat Cheese & Olive Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared salmon sits centrally on a round, rustic ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The salmon fillet, with its golden-brown, crispy skin and flaky, pink interior, is placed on a generous bed of vibrant mixed salad greens. Interspersed among the greens are dark purple-black Kalamata olive halves and creamy white crumbles of goat cheese, creating a pleasing color contrast. A light sheen of hot sauce vinaigrette coats the salad components, adding a subtle glisten. The arrangement is casual and organic, allowing ingredients to naturally overlap. The plate rests on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen light. A simple, folded linen napkin and a fork are placed beside the plate. The overall scene evokes a comfortable, home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear salmon skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until crispy. Flip.
Cook for another 3-5 minutes until desired doneness. Remove from pan.
In a small bowl, whisk remaining 40ml olive oil, hot sauce, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine salad greens, halved olives, and crumbled goat cheese.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to coat.
Divide salad among 4 plates. Top each with a seared salmon fillet. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Smoked Meat and Cheese Strata
recipes.visual_description: A generous square portion of the strata rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features a rich, golden-brown crust, revealing soft, custard-soaked bread cubes beneath. Layers of savory diced smoked ham and turkey are intertwined with crumbled, browned pork sausage. Pockets of creamy, melted cheese are visible throughout the interior. Fresh, vibrant red tomato slices, slightly caramelized from baking, adorn the top surface. The overall color palette is warm, with golden browns, creamy whites, and the deep reds of tomato, accented by green parsley. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the strata. The plate is centered on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin sits beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its varied textures. The background shows a soft-focus, casual modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a side of mixed green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x30cm baking dish.
Dice smoked ham and smoked turkey into small cubes. Crumble feta cheese.
Cook pork sausage in a large pan over medium heat until browned and cooked through. Crumble the sausage. Drain excess fat.
Melt butter in the same pan. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, egg whites, milk, yogurt, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper until well combined.
In another bowl, combine shredded cheddar, softened cream cheese, cottage cheese, and crumbled feta.
Cut rustic bread into 2-3cm cubes. Place half of the bread cubes evenly in the prepared baking dish.
Layer cooked sausage, diced ham, and diced turkey over the bread.
Evenly spread half of the combined cheese mixture over the meats.
Add the remaining bread cubes on top of the cheese layer.
Spread the remaining meat and cheese mixture over the top bread layer.
Carefully pour the egg mixture evenly over all layers. Gently press down with a spatula to ensure bread is soaked.
Slice the tomato into thin rounds. Arrange tomato slices decoratively on top of the strata.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally overnight, for best flavor and texture.

Bake covered for 30 minutes. Uncover and continue baking for 20-30 minutes, or until the strata is golden brown on top, puffed, and set. An inserted knife should come out clean. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes before serving.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the strata generously with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: For best results, prepare the strata the night before and refrigerate it overnight. This allows the bread to fully absorb the egg custard, resulting in a more uniform and tender texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Cherry Upside-Down Cake
recipes.visual_description: A generous slice of Cherry Upside-Down Cake rests on an everyday ceramic plate. The cake shows a golden-brown, tender crumb on the bottom. The top is covered with a glossy, rich caramelized layer featuring whole and halved dark red cooked cherries, their natural shapes visible. Some of the warm, amber caramel drips slightly down the sides of the cherries. The cake is moist and appears freshly baked. The plate is positioned casually on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a family kitchen setting. A simple, casually placed cloth napkin is nearby. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, comfortable atmosphere. A portion of the whole cake, resting on a simple cake stand, is visible in the background, reinforcing the homely feel.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease a 20 cm round cake pan with butter.
Pour 50 g of melted butter into the prepared pan. Sprinkle brown sugar evenly over the butter.
Arrange pitted cherries in a single layer over the brown sugar. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg, milk, remaining 65 g melted butter, and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Carefully spoon the cake batter over the cherries in the pan. Spread evenly.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let the cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes on a wire rack.
Place a serving plate upside down over the cake pan. Invert the cake onto the plate. Remove the pan.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Ginger Scallion Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Ginger Scallion Fried Rice is mounded neatly in the center of a clean, round white porcelain plate. The rice is golden-brown, showing distinct grains, with some lightly crisped edges from frying. Diced chicken pieces are interspersed throughout, appearing fully cooked with a slight golden sear. Vibrant green peas and small, bright orange diced carrots add pops of color. Specks of fresh, thinly sliced green onion are visible. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of additional fresh green onion slices and a subtle sheen from sesame oil. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space around the central mound. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and a pair of dark chopsticks resting next to a small, empty white ceramic rice bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, authentic Chinese dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with chopsticks and individual ceramic rice bowls.
Offer a side of chili oil or a light clear broth.

ingredients.name: Chicken breast or thigh, diced into 1.5 cm cubes
Large green onions, white and green parts separated, sliced
Carrot, peeled and diced into 0.5 cm cubes

instructions: Pat diced chicken dry. Season with a pinch of salt and 15 ml soy sauce.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add chicken. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until cooked through and lightly golden. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add another 10 ml oil to the wok. Pour in beaten eggs. Scramble until just set. Break into small pieces. Remove eggs and set aside.
Add remaining 20 ml oil to the wok. Add minced ginger, minced garlic, and white parts of green onions. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced carrots. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.

Add the cold day-old rice to the wok. Break up any clumps with a spatula. Press rice against the hot surface to fry. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is heated through and slightly crispy.
Return cooked chicken and scrambled eggs to the wok. Add frozen peas.
Pour remaining 45 ml soy sauce over the rice. Sprinkle with white pepper. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes to combine all ingredients and evenly distribute seasonings.
Add the green parts of the green onions. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with toasted sesame oil. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately.
notes: Using day-old, chilled rice is crucial for the best fried rice texture, preventing it from becoming mushy.
Cook at high heat to achieve a slightly smoky 'wok hei' flavor and prevent steaming.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Chicken Adobo with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Filipino Chicken Adobo with Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dish features several whole, tender braised chicken thighs, rich brown from the adobo sauce. Alongside are thick, rustic chunks of fork-tender potatoes, also imbued with the glossy, dark amber sauce. The sauce, thickened slightly, coats the chicken and potatoes, reflecting the light. A few whole black peppercorns are visible, adding texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with a small mound of fluffy white steamed rice in a traditional rice bowl and a fresh green cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the deep, savory colors of the dish. A small bowl of vibrant green pickled papaya (atchara) is placed to the side, providing a contrasting color and cultural element. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed white rice.
Traditionally accompanied by a side of pickled green papaya (atchara) to balance the richness.
Often eaten family-style, with individual portions of rice.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced white onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in soy sauce, cane vinegar, water or chicken broth. Add bay leaves and black peppercorns.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Bring liquid to a simmer.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add peeled and quartered potatoes to the pot. Stir gently.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 20-25 minutes. Cook until chicken is tender and potatoes are fork-tender. Internal temperature of chicken should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot.
notes: Do not stir the adobo mixture immediately after adding the vinegar; allow it to simmer for a few minutes before stirring to let the sourness mellow.
The sauce should be savory with a distinct tang from the vinegar, balanced by the soy sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Sausage and Ham Gratin with Feta and Herb Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of the Creamy Sausage and Ham Gratin is presented in a clean, white oval gratin dish, or as a well-defined scoop on a simple round white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin boasts a rich, bubbly, golden-brown crust, indicating a perfectly baked, cheesy top layer. Visible through the melted cheese are crumbles of browned sausage and small, pink cubes of smoked ham, embedded within a creamy, pale yellow custard base. A distinct dollop of bright white, thick herb yogurt sits artfully on one side, lightly dusted with finely chopped fresh green chives and parsley. The overall composition is inviting and hearty, with a balance of warm golden tones and fresh green accents, offering a satisfying texture contrast. The dish is set on a light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded light gray cotton napkin and simple silver flatware, under even, natural lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Remove sausage from casings. Crumble sausage into a large skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until browned. Drain excess fat. Transfer sausage to a large bowl.
Dice smoked ham into small cubes. Add to the skillet. Cook until lightly browned. Transfer ham to the bowl with sausage.
Add olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add to the meat mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk together softened cream cheese, cottage cheese, 2 large eggs, 1 egg white, and milk until smooth. Stir in grated Gruyère or Cheddar cheese, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the cheese and egg mixture over the meat and onion in the large bowl. Stir to combine thoroughly.
Pour the entire mixture into the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the gratin is set, bubbly, and golden brown on top.
While the gratin bakes, combine plain yogurt with half of the chopped fresh parsley and chives. Season with a pinch of salt.
Remove gratin from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve individual portions of the gratin with a dollop of the herb yogurt on top or beside. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Tenderloin with Cherry-Port Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of succulent pork tenderloin medallions rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each medallion, about 2-3 cm thick, reveals a perfectly cooked, pale pink interior with a golden-brown seared crust. A generous pool of glossy, deep ruby-red cherry-port reduction sauce cascades around the pork, studded with plump, soft pitted cherries. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered artfully over the sauce for a touch of green. The plate sits on a warm, natural wood table surface. A simple grey cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in soft, even natural light, creating a professional yet inviting casual dining atmosphere.
instructions: Pat pork tenderloins dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork tenderloins on all sides until golden brown. This takes about 6-8 minutes.

Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 65°C (149°F). Remove pork from pan. Let rest on a cutting board, loosely covered, for 10 minutes.
While pork rests, make the sauce. In the same pan, add butter. Sauté diced shallots until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add pitted cherries and chicken stock. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, until cherries soften and sauce slightly thickens.
Remove thyme sprigs. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Slice pork tenderloin into 2-3 cm thick medallions.
Serve pork medallions with cherry-port reduction.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomato-Basil Sauce is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The seared chicken thigh, with its golden-brown crust, is placed centrally on the plate. Beside the chicken, several golden-brown roasted potato wedges are arranged neatly. A vibrant, rich red tomato-basil sauce is generously spooned over the chicken and partially coats the potatoes, creating a pleasing contrast. The sauce contains visible flecks of green basil and soft, diced tomatoes. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the dish as a final garnish, adding a pop of color. The textures are varied: crispy chicken skin, tender chicken meat, fluffy interior of the potatoes, and the smooth, rustic sauce. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the food without harsh shadows. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
A side of simple green salad with vinaigrette.
A glass of dry white wine or light red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2.5 cm wedges or chunks. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Flip halfway through.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in fresh basil leaves, roughly torn. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken over roasted potatoes. Spoon tomato-basil sauce generously over chicken and potatoes. Garnish with additional fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust seasoning of sauce to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Carne Deshebrada (Mexican Shredded Beef)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Carne Deshebrada is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a mound of rich, reddish-brown shredded beef. The beef is loosely piled in the center, allowing some of the thick, savory tomato-chile sauce to pool naturally around its base. The texture of the beef is tender and fibrous, coated in the vibrant sauce. Garnishes include a scattering of finely diced white onion and a generous amount of fresh, bright green cilantro leaves over the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. A lime wedge is placed neatly beside the beef. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. In the background, a small, rustic woven basket holds warm corn tortillas. A small ceramic ramekin of salsa roja is visible. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style atmosphere. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the main subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for making tacos or sopes
Offer various salsas (e.g., salsa roja, salsa verde) on the side
Serve with a side of refried beans or Mexican rice
instructions: Cut beef chuck roast into 5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Remove stems and seeds from dried ancho and chipotle chiles. Place chiles in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let soak for 20 minutes until softened.
While chiles soak, slice one onion thinly. Add to the pot. Cook until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add to pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Drain softened chiles. Add chiles, diced tomatoes, cumin, and oregano to a blender. Add 125 ml of beef broth. Blend until smooth.
Pour chile mixture into the pot with onions and garlic. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add remaining beef broth and bay leaf. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from pot. Shred beef using two forks. Discard bay leaf.
If sauce is too thin, simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes until desired consistency. Stir shredded beef back into the sauce.
Finely dice remaining white onion. Chop fresh cilantro.
Serve carne deshebrada hot with warm corn tortillas, diced white onion, and fresh cilantro. Offer lime wedges on the side.
notes: For extra spice, add a serrano or jalapeño pepper to the blender with the chiles.
The beef can be cooked in a slow cooker on low for 6-8 hours or high for 3-4 hours after searing and sauce preparation.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Root Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hearty Chicken and Root Vegetable Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. The soup fills the bowl, showcasing chunky, irregular 1.5 cm diced pieces of tender potato, vibrant orange carrots, and pale green celery, along with substantial 2 cm chunks of cooked chicken. The broth is a comforting, golden hue. A light scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley rests on the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall arrangement is natural and casual, as if served in a home kitchen. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is casually draped beside the bowl. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in family dining area with subtle, unobtrusive elements like a simple salt and pepper shaker set. The entire bowl is visible, with adequate negative space around it.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery into 1.5 cm cubes. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Add diced potatoes, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Return seared chicken to the pot. Simmer, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken & Beef with Spiced Buckwheat Rice, Herb Yogurt, and Fresh Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a balanced and approachable composition. At the center is a mound of fluffy, golden-brown spiced buckwheat rice, its grains distinct and glistening. Nestled beside the rice are a whole, pan-seared chicken breast, its skin a rich golden-brown, and several thick, seared beef chunks with a deep brown crust and hints of pink interior. A generous dollop of creamy white herb yogurt sauce rests beside the proteins, with a light drizzle extending onto the grains. A perfectly fried egg, its vibrant yellow yolk contrasting with crisp white edges, sits atop the buckwheat rice. To the side, a small, neat pile of bright green diced cucumber and crisp white apple cubes adds a fresh, vibrant pop of color and texture. Two to three thin, subtly caramelized banana slices, with a light golden hue, are artfully placed near the proteins. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh green dill and parsley, adding freshness. A lemon wedge and a slice of rustic crusty bread complete the presentation. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a clean white cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the food while maintaining a casual, inviting atmosphere.
instructions: Rinse rice and buckwheat separately. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot. Add half diced onion, cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add rice and buckwheat, stir 1 minute. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and grains are tender. Stir in 15g butter. Keep warm.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season chicken and beef all over with salt and black pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, let rest. Add beef to hot skillet. Sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Remove beef, let rest 5 minutes. Slice beef into 2cm thick chunks or medallions. Leave chicken breasts whole or slice into two thick pieces.
In a bowl, combine Greek yogurt, milk, lemon juice, half chopped dill, and half chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Dice cucumber and apple into 1cm cubes. In a small bowl, combine diced cucumber and apple. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

Peel banana. Slice into 0.5cm thick rounds. Heat a small non-stick pan over medium heat. Add banana slices. Cook 1-2 minutes per side until lightly caramelized. Season with a tiny pinch of salt and red pepper flakes (if using).
Fry 4 eggs in the same skillet used for proteins until whites are set and yolks are runny or to your preference. Season with salt and pepper.

Spoon a generous portion of spiced buckwheat rice onto each plate. Arrange seared chicken and beef chunks/medallions beside the grains. Place a fried egg on top of or next to the grains. Spoon a dollop of herb yogurt next to the proteins, or drizzle over. Place a small mound of apple-cucumber salad on the plate. Arrange 2-3 slices of savory banana next to the proteins. Garnish with remaining fresh dill and parsley. Serve with a lemon wedge and a slice of crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown seared chicken thighs rest on a generous bed of reddish-orange rice. The rice is fluffy, with distinct grains, interspersed with soft, diced red tomatoes and tender, caramelized onion pieces. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a bright contrast. The dish is presented on a round, rustic cream-colored ceramic plate, filling it with a hearty, home-style portion. The plate sits on a well-used, light wooden kitchen table. A simple, silver fork and knife are placed casually beside the plate, with a slightly crumpled plain linen napkin. Soft, warm overhead lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The background subtly suggests a lived-in family kitchen, with natural, minimal clutter.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip. Sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly toasted.
Pour in diced tomatoes (undrained) and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure liquid almost covers chicken.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Turkey & Root Vegetable Bowl with Quick-Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the Braised Turkey & Root Vegetable Bowl rests in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl of natural, earthy beige. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center on a light, reclaimed wood table. A generous bed of roasted root vegetables—chunks of golden potato, orange carrot, and pale parsnip—display tender, caramelized edges. Interspersed are crisp, halved Brussels sprouts, their vibrant green contrasting with softer interiors. Substantial, pulled chunks of dark turkey meat are centrally placed, showcasing its tender texture. A light sheen of reduced braising liquid coats the turkey. To one side, a small, vibrant pile of thinly sliced quick-pickled red onions adds a pop of fuchsia. A few fresh rosemary sprigs are tucked among the ingredients. The composition is clean, with ample white space, emphasizing each ingredient's pure beauty. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting organic textures. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the bowl.

ingredients.name: Carrots, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks
Parsnips, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks
Potatoes, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks
Turkey broth or low-sodium chicken broth

instructions: Prepare Pickled Onions: In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, 5g salt, peppercorns, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar or bowl. Pour hot brine over onions. Let cool, then cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Braise Turkey: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat turkey thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. In a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven, heat 30 ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear turkey thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear for another 3 minutes. Remove turkey from pot.

Braise Turkey (continued): Add rosemary and thyme sprigs to the pot. Deglaze with turkey broth, scraping up any browned bits. Return turkey thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Bring to a simmer. Cover tightly and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until turkey is very tender and pulls easily from the bone.

Roast Vegetables: While turkey braises, toss carrots, parsnips, and potatoes with remaining 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a large baking sheet. Roast in the oven with the turkey for the last 45-60 minutes of turkey cooking time, or until tender and lightly browned. Add Brussels sprouts to the baking sheet for the last 20 minutes of roasting, tossing with vegetables.

Finish Turkey: Once braised, remove turkey thighs from the pot. Discard skin and bones. Shred or pull turkey meat into large, rustic chunks. Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Reduce braising liquid over medium-high heat on the stovetop until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes.

Assemble and Serve: Divide roasted root vegetables and Brussels sprouts among 4 individual serving bowls. Place generous chunks of braised turkey on top of the vegetables. Spoon some reduced braising liquid over the turkey and vegetables. Garnish each bowl with a small pile of quick-pickled red onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage, Tomato, and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Sausage, Tomato, and Mushroom Risotto is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. The risotto is fluid and creamy, spreading slightly in the bowl, showcasing its rich, pale orange-red hue from the crushed tomatoes. Prominently visible are rustic, browned chunks of savory Italian sausage, tender sliced cremini mushrooms, and creamy white cannellini beans, all evenly dispersed within the al dente rice grains. A sprinkle of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese melts gently on top, accompanied by a small cluster of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The setting is a modern bistro, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual dining atmosphere. A simple silver fork and spoon are placed neatly beside the bowl on a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, emphasizing its comforting yet refined appeal. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Serve with crusty bread to soak up any remaining creamy sauce.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into bite-sized chunks.

Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Brown thoroughly, breaking up with a spoon. Remove sausage to a plate, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
Dice onion. Add to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Mince garlic. Add to the pot, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Slice mushrooms. Add to the pot. Sauté until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice until edges become translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Add one ladle of warm broth to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is almost fully absorbed. Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
Drain and rinse cannellini beans. When risotto is almost al dente (after about 15 minutes of broth additions), stir in the cooked sausage and cannellini beans.
Continue adding broth until rice is creamy and al dente, with a slight bite in the center. The risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove pot from heat. Add butter and 70 g of the grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and the risotto is very creamy (mantecatura).
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Let risotto rest for 2 minutes, covered.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish each serving with fresh chopped parsley and the remaining grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure broth is kept warm throughout the cooking process to maintain rice temperature and promote even cooking.
Adjust the amount of broth to achieve desired creamy, fluid consistency; not all broth may be needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chickpea Dal with Spiced Root-to-Stem Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Fermented Chickpea Dal is served in a handcrafted, deep cream-colored ceramic bowl with a subtle matte finish. The dal, a rich golden-yellow, is thick and comforting, with visible whole chickpeas, soft diced tomatoes, and tender pieces of green root-to-stem vegetables. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh coriander leaves provides a fresh contrast on top. A few whole, toasted black cumin seeds and slivers of red dried chili are visible. The bowl rests on a light, natural reclaimed wood surface with visible grain. Adjacent to the bowl, a small, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually folded. A small, rustic ceramic side dish holds a few extra pieces of vibrant, roughly chopped fermented vegetable pickle. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, whole-wheat flatbread (roti or chapati)
Serve with steamed brown rice
Offer a side of plain yogurt or a simple cucumber raita

ingredients.name: Seasonal Root-to-Stem Vegetables (e.g., carrot tops, radish greens, cauliflower leaves)
Fermented Vegetable Pickle (e.g., lacto-fermented carrots or radishes)

instructions: Rinse chickpea dal thoroughly. Soak dal in water for 4-6 hours, or overnight.
Drain soaked dal. Place dal in a large pot with 1.5 litres fresh water. Bring to a boil. Skim any foam.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer dal for 45-60 minutes until tender. Dal should be soft.
Heat oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Add black cumin seeds and dried red chilies. Sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add diced onion and minced garlic. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add grated ginger, turmeric powder, and coriander powder. Cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chopped root-to-stem vegetables. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Pour the cooked dal into the vegetable mixture. Add vegetable stock. Stir well.
Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Add water if dal becomes too thick.
Stir in the roughly chopped fermented vegetable pickle. Cook for 2 minutes.
Season with salt to taste. Squeeze fresh lemon or lime juice.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
notes: This recipe prioritizes using vegetable scraps and fermented elements to minimize food waste and enhance flavor complexity.
Adjust dried red chili quantity to personal heat preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Creamy Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homestyle Creamy Chicken and Rice is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Diced chicken pieces, approximately 2-3 cm, are cooked until golden and nestled among fluffy, creamy rice, enriched by diced carrots and tender pieces of tomato. The dish has a warm, inviting golden-orange hue from the tomato and coconut milk, with visible specks of green from a light parsley garnish. The texture is soft and comforting, with the rice absorbing the rich, savory sauce. A casual cloth napkin is loosely placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy light emanates from an overhead kitchen fixture, highlighting the dish's comforting appeal. The scene is uncluttered, focusing solely on the hearty, expertly prepared meal.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Dice onion and carrot into small cubes. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Brown on all sides, about 5 minutes. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrot to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and Dijon mustard. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add uncooked rice to the pot. Stir to coat the grains.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return browned chicken to the pot. Stir gently to combine.
Cover the pot, reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and creamy.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Italian Sausage and Bean Ragù
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hearty Italian Sausage and Bean Ragù is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. The ragù is a rich, deep red from the crushed tomatoes, studded with substantial, rustic chunks of browned Italian sausage and tender, earthy sliced mushrooms. Whole or halved cannellini beans are visibly integrated, adding a creamy contrast. The dish is topped with a generous sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese and vibrant green chopped parsley, offering fresh color and texture. The composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into 2-3 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Brown on all sides, about 8 minutes. Remove sausage from pot; set aside.
Dice the onion. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook until browned, about 7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is mostly reduced, about 3 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return sausage chunks to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently, uncovered, for 20 minutes.
Drain and rinse cannellini beans. Add beans to the pot. Stir well. Simmer for another 10 minutes.
Grate Parmesan cheese. Stir half of the grated Parmesan into the ragù. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
